mainTopic: A בכור that fell into a pit on יום טוב: examining blemishes, the ban on tricks, מוקצה, and the parallel ברייתא
overview: This עמוד finishes the משנה about a בכור (firstborn animal) that fell into a pit on יום טוב. A בכור may only be slaughtered and eaten if it has a permanent מום (blemish). רבי יהודה says that if it has a מום, it may be lifted out and slaughtered; if not, it may not be slaughtered. רבי שמעון says that if the מום was not known before יום טוב, the animal is not מוכן (prepared) and may not be slaughtered. The גמרא suggests they argue about whether blemishes may be examined on יום טוב. It explains that the pit case adds a lesson: one may not use a trick (ערמה) to lift out a בכור that cannot be slaughtered, even to spare it pain. Through several challenges (it is תם; it is מוקצה), the גמרא settles on the משנה's real case: a temporary מום before יום טוב that became permanent on יום טוב. Even then, the animal is מוקצה and may not be slaughtered. Finally, a ברייתא records רבי יהודה הנשיא allowing an expert to go down and examine the animal, and רבי שמעון בן מנסיא objects that blemishes are not examined on יום טוב. His explanation continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's ruling: slaughter only if it has a blemish
steps.stepSummary: The end of רבי יהודה's view in the משנה: if the fallen בכור has a מום, it may be lifted out and slaughtered; if not, it may not be slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it has a blemish, he may lift it up and slaughter it. If not, he may not slaughter it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes רבי יהודה's ruling (begun on the previous דף) about a בכור that fell into a pit on יום טוב. After an expert checks it, the outcome depends on whether a blemish is found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור belongs to the כהן and may only be slaughtered for ordinary eating if it has a permanent מום. So the check decides everything. With a מום, it is food for יום טוב and may be lifted and slaughtered. Without one, it cannot be slaughtered, so there is no יום טוב-food reason to lift it out.

keyTerms.meaning: A physical blemish. A permanent one allows a בכור to be slaughtered and eaten outside the מקדש.
He may lift it up (out of the pit).
He may slaughter it.
And if not.

phrases.english: If it has a blemish,
phrases.notes: The subject is the בכור that fell into a pit, mentioned at the start of the משנה.

phrases.english: he may raise it and slaughter it;
phrases.notes: Because it is now fit to eat on יום טוב.

phrases.english: and if not, he may not slaughter it.
phrases.notes: No blemish (or only a temporary one) means it cannot be eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from the previous דף (רבי יהודה: an expert goes down and checks).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, a fallen בכור found to have a מום on יום טוב may be raised and slaughtered; without a מום it may not be slaughtered.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's ruling: a blemish not known before יום טוב makes the animal unprepared
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון rules that any בכור whose blemish was not recognized before יום טוב is not מוכן, so it may not be slaughtered on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: Any animal whose blemish was not recognized while it was still day (before יום טוב) is not considered prepared.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון disagrees with רבי יהודה. He says that even if a blemish is found now, the animal may not be slaughtered, because nobody knew about the blemish before יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום טוב, one may only use things that were ready for use (מוכן) before the holiday began. Before יום טוב this בכור was not known to be permitted, so no one had it in mind as food. Finding the blemish today is too late.

keyTerms.meaning: Recognizable or known.
While it was still day, meaning before יום טוב began.
Prepared, meaning designated or fit for use before יום טוב began.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the concept of מוכן and מוקצה that runs through all of מסכת ביצה: things not ready before יום טוב may not be used on it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
any animal whose blemish is not recognizable
while it is still day (before the Festival),
this is not among the prepared (animals).
phrases.notes: So it may not be slaughtered on יום טוב, even if it does have a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי יהודה's ruling in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, a בכור whose blemish was not known before יום טוב is not מוכן and may not be slaughtered on יום טוב.

steps.title: What exactly are they arguing about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the underlying principle behind the מחלוקת of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks what deeper principle divides רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון. This question sets up the next move, where the גמרא will try out an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants to find the general rule behind a specific case. Once it knows the principle, it can ask whether the משנה chose the best example to teach it.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree?

phrases.english: GEMARA:
With regard to what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the principle behind the two rulings of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying legal principle on which רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון disagree.

steps.title: If the argument is about checking blemishes, why choose a pit case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests they argue about whether one may examine blemishes on יום טוב. It then objects: if so, they should have argued about examining blemishes in general, not specifically about a בכור in a pit.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say they disagree about examining blemishes, so that רבי יהודה holds one may examine blemishes on יום טוב and רבי שמעון holds one may not, then let them disagree about examining blemishes in general!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer: the argument is about whether an expert may examine an animal's blemishes on יום טוב. It then challenges that answer: why tie this to a pit, when the issue applies to any בכור?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the only issue were רואין מומין ביום טוב, the pit detail adds nothing. The simpler way to teach it would be a regular בכור examined on יום טוב. So the pit detail must be there for a reason, and the גמרא demands to know what it is.

keyTerms.meaning: One may examine blemishes (an expert may inspect an animal to declare it blemished).
If we say (introduces a suggested explanation).
So let them disagree (about a different, broader case).
In general, the ordinary case.

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not reject the idea that they argue about רואין מומין. It only asks why the משנה used the pit case to show it. The answer in the next step keeps the idea and explains what the pit adds.

phrases.english: If we say they disagree about examining blemishes,
that Rabbi Yehuda holds:
one may examine blemishes on a Festival,
and Rabbi Shimon holds:
one may not examine blemishes on a Festival,
then let them disagree about examining blemishes in general!
phrases.notes: Why bring in a בכור that fell into a pit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a candidate answer to step 3's question and immediately challenges the משנה's choice of case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's choice of the specific case of a בכור in a pit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the argument is only about רואין מומין ביום טוב, the pit detail is unnecessary. A general case would teach the same thing more simply.

steps.title: The pit case teaches that no trick may be used to lift it out
steps.stepSummary: The pit case was needed. Otherwise we might think that, because of צער בעלי חיים, one may lift out a blemish-free בכור using a trick, following רבי יהושע. The משנה teaches that this is not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case of a בכור that fell into a pit was needed. You might have thought that, because of the suffering of animals, one may use a trick and lift it out, like רבי יהושע. So the משנה teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the pit adds a new lesson. When the בכור has no blemish, we may not use a trick to lift it out, even though the animal is suffering in the pit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Elsewhere רבי יהושע allows a trick (ערמה) to rescue an animal from a pit on יום טוב: one lifts it 'in order to slaughter it' and then does not slaughter it. We might have applied that here to spare the בכור. The משנה's ruling 'ואם לאו לא ישחוט' teaches that for a blemish-free בכור, even this trick is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary for him (to teach this case).
It would have entered your mind to say (introduces a mistaken assumption).
The suffering of living creatures; the Torah's concern about causing pain to animals.
To use a trick or legal pretext (ערמה).
It teaches us (a new lesson).

steps.confusionAlert: The new lesson is in the 'if not' half of the ruling (no blemish). It is not about the animal that has a blemish. Do not think the משנה forbids rescuing animals in general; it forbids a trick for a בכור that cannot be slaughtered.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that צער בעלי חיים does not automatically override the rules of יום טוב when the only way to permit the rescue is a pretext that cannot be fulfilled.

phrases.english: The case of a firstborn that fell into a pit was necessary,
for it would have entered your mind to say:
because of the suffering of living creatures,
one may use a trick and raise it up,
in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua;
phrases.notes: רבי יהושע (later in the מסכת) allows a trick to rescue an animal from a pit on יום טוב.

phrases.english: so it teaches us (that this is not allowed).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4 by showing that the pit detail adds its own lesson.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains a necessary detail (אצטריכא): the specific case teaches an extra lesson.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because of צער בעלי חיים, one might use רבי יהושע's trick to lift out even a blemish-free בכור.
steps.terutzMaskana: No trick may be used to lift out a blemish-free בכור on יום טוב.

steps.title: Then the משנה should have said 'he may not raise it'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer from the wording. If the lesson is about not lifting the animal out, the משנה should say 'he may not raise it and slaughter it,' not just 'he may not slaughter it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does it say 'he may not slaughter'? It should have said 'he may not raise it and slaughter it!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the previous answer against the exact words of the משנה. The answer was about lifting the animal, but the משנה only mentions slaughtering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said the lesson is that one may not lift the animal out with a trick. But the משנה's words 'לא ישחוט' speak only about slaughtering. The wording does not seem to match the explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your explanation is right).
It should have said.

phrases.english: If so, (why does it say) 'he may not slaughter'?
It should have said 'he may not raise it and slaughter it'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 5 from the wording of the משנה in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation in step 5 that the משנה forbids using a trick to lift the animal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the lesson is about lifting, the משנה's wording should forbid lifting ('לא יעלה'), not only slaughtering.

steps.title: Even if he already lifted it out, he may not slaughter it
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is speaking about someone who broke the rule and already lifted the בכור out. One might think he may now slaughter it, so the משנה teaches that he may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for a case where he went ahead and lifted it out. You might have thought he may now slaughter it, so the משנה teaches us that he may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the wording: 'לא ישחוט' covers the case where the animal was already lifted out improperly. Even then, slaughtering is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on lifting is assumed; the משנה adds a further point. Once the animal is out of the pit, one might think that slaughtering it would at least justify the lifting after the fact. The משנה rules that a blemish-free בכור may still not be slaughtered.

keyTerms.meaning: No, it is needed (for a specific case).
Where he transgressed (already did the forbidden act).
And lifted it up.

phrases.english: No, it is necessary
where he transgressed and raised it,
for it would have entered your mind to say: he may slaughter it;
so it teaches us (that he may not).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of step 6 by narrowing the case to after-the-fact lifting.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case narrowly (לא צריכא): the משנה speaks about after the fact (בדיעבד).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once the animal was already lifted out, one might think it may now be slaughtered.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even after it was improperly lifted out, a blemish-free בכור may not be slaughtered on יום טוב.

steps.title: Why would anyone think an unblemished בכור may be slaughtered?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא wonders at the previous answer. A בכור with no blemish (תם) may never be slaughtered outside the מקדש, so why would the משנה need to say so?
steps.simpleTranslation: He may slaughter it?! But it is unblemished!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 7. It asks why anyone would ever think it is allowed to slaughter a בכור that has no blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור that is תם is holy and may not be slaughtered for ordinary eating at all. So no one would think lifting it out makes it permitted. That makes the משנה's lesson seem pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him slaughter it (said here with surprise)
Unblemished (a בכור with no blemish)
But look, isn't it

phrases.english: He may slaughter it?!
But it is unblemished!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 7's claim that the משנה teaches you may not slaughter the בכור after lifting it out
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A תם בכור is never permitted to be slaughtered, so no one would need to be told this.

steps.title: The animal got a blemish after it fell
steps.stepSummary: The case is one where the בכור developed a blemish, for example from the fall, so slaughtering it would normally be allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only where a blemish developed in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing the case. The בכור is not unblemished anymore, because it got a blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור with a permanent מום may be slaughtered and eaten. So there is now a real reason to think it might be allowed, and the משנה's ruling teaches something.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for (a specific case)
A blemish

phrases.english: It is needed only
where a blemish developed in it.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since it now has a blemish, perhaps he may slaughter it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה teaches he still may not.

steps.title: But the animal is מוקצה
steps.stepSummary: Even with a new blemish, the animal was forbidden when יום טוב began. That makes it מוקצה for the whole day, so no one would think to slaughter it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new answer. An animal that got its blemish only on יום טוב is obviously מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When יום טוב started, the בכור was unblemished and could not be eaten, so the owner never set it aside as food. Something not ready at the start of יום טוב stays מוקצה all day. So again there is no reason to think it may be slaughtered.

keyTerms.meaning: Set aside: not available for use on יום טוב because it was not ready when the day began
But isn't it

steps.confusionAlert: The problem here is not the holiness of the בכור. The blemish already solved that. The problem is the יום טוב rule of מוקצה: the animal was not usable when the day began.

phrases.english: But it is muktze!

steps.kashyaTarget: The case of a blemish that developed on יום טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since it was unfit when יום טוב began, it is plainly מוקצה. No one would think to permit it, so the משנה's lesson would be obvious.

steps.title: A temporary blemish before יום טוב became permanent on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The animal already had a temporary blemish (מום עובר) before יום טוב, and on יום טוב it became a permanent blemish (מום קבוע). One might think the owner already had it in mind as food, so it is not מוקצה. The משנה teaches that it is still forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is where a temporary blemish developed in it before יום טוב, and now it has become a permanent blemish. You might have said: his mind was on it, so he may slaughter it. The משנה teaches us that he may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a better case, where it is a real question whether the animal is מוקצה. It concludes that the משנה forbids it anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a temporary blemish before יום טוב, the owner might have expected it to become permanent and thought about eating the animal. That could make it not מוקצה. The משנה teaches that this is not enough: since the animal was not actually fit before יום טוב, it remains מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: A temporary blemish that may heal (does not permit slaughter)
A permanent blemish (permits slaughtering a בכור)
You might have said (introduces the mistaken thought)
His mind was set on it
It teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's case: a בכור with a temporary blemish before יום טוב that became permanent on יום טוב, after it fell into a pit. Even though the owner may have had it in mind, it is מוקצה and may not be slaughtered.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that just having something in mind does not remove מוקצה when the item was actually forbidden at the start of יום טוב.

phrases.english: Rather: where a temporary blemish developed in it
from the eve of the Festival,
and now it has become a permanent blemish.
You might have said: since his mind was on it,
let him slaughter it. It teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דִּנְפַל בֵּיהּ מוּם עוֹבֵר מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer of Step 9 after the challenge in Step 10
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since he had the animal in mind before יום טוב because of its temporary blemish, it is not מוקצה and he may slaughter it.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is still מוקצה, because it was not fit before יום טוב, so he may not slaughter it.

steps.title: The ברייתא: רבי יהודה הנשיא allows an expert to go down and examine
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings a dispute about an unblemished בכור that fell into a pit. רבי יהודה הנשיא says an expert goes down and examines it. If it has a blemish, they raise it and slaughter it. If not, it is not slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: about an unblemished בכור that fell into a pit, רבי יהודה הנשיא says: an expert goes down and looks. If it has a blemish, he raises it and slaughters it. If not, he does not slaughter it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא, a teaching from outside the משנה, on the same case. It records רבי יהודה הנשיא's view first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה הנשיא allows checking for a blemish on יום טוב itself. He also ties lifting the animal out to slaughtering it: raise it only if it will be slaughtered. If no blemish is found, it may not be slaughtered.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught (introduces a ברייתא)
An expert who judges blemishes
He will look / examine
Pit / cistern

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
An unblemished firstborn that fell into a pit,
Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says:
An expert goes down and examines it,

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ בּוֹ מוּם — יַעֲלֶה וְיִשְׁחוֹט,
phrases.english: if it has a blemish, he raises it and slaughters it,
and if not, he does not slaughter it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן בְּכוֹר תָּם שֶׁנָּפַל לַבּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא on the same case as the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An expert may examine a בכור in a pit on יום טוב. If it has a blemish, it is raised and slaughtered. If not, it is not slaughtered.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא: blemishes are not examined on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא objects that the earlier חכמים ruled that blemishes are not examined on יום טוב. He then begins to explain: a blemish that appeared before יום טוב may not be checked on יום טוב. The next case is cut off at the end of the עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא said to him: They already said that blemishes are not examined on יום טוב. How so? If a blemish appeared before יום טוב, it is not checked on יום טוב. If a blemish appeared...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא challenges רבי יהודה הנשיא with an accepted rule. He then starts explaining that rule case by case, and the explanation continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה הנשיא's ruling depends on examining blemishes on יום טוב. רבי שמעון בן מנסיא cites a known rule that this is forbidden. The 'כיצד' section shows the rule applies even to a blemish that already existed before יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: They have already said (citing an accepted rule)
One does not examine blemishes
How so? (introduces details)
Inspect / check

steps.confusionAlert: The text breaks off in the middle at 'נולד בו מום'. The second case (a blemish that appeared on יום טוב itself) continues on the next עמוד.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן מְנַסְיָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya said to him:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי אָמְרוּ אֵין רוֹאִין מוּמִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: They already said: one does not examine blemishes on a Festival.
How so?

phrases.aramaic: נוֹלַד בּוֹ מוּם מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: If a blemish appeared in it on the eve of the Festival,
one does not inspect it on the Festival.
If a blemish appeared in it
phrases.notes: Sentence continues on the next עמוד

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן מְנַסְיָא הֲרֵי אָמְרוּ אֵין רוֹאִין מוּמִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Objects to רבי יהודה הנשיא's ruling within the ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה הנשיא's permission for an expert to examine the בכור on יום טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is an accepted rule that blemishes are not examined on יום טוב, even a blemish from before יום טוב, so the expert may not examine it.
